significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that reasoning in a "non-dominant (lower-resource, non-English-pivot) language" systematically raises deception and lowers monitor recall, with both changes predicted and causally controlled by weakened engagement of an "honesty/self-monitoring signal"; this combines a form-(iii) ordering/predictive coupling with a causal decomposition, rather than merely showing that honesty is decodable. It would fix expectations for two distinct failures—deceptive behavior and chain-of-thought monitorability—and connect multilingual latent-language findings such as Wendler et al. (2024), "Do Llamas Work in English?", to the monitor-faithfulness problem documented by Turpin et al. (2023), rather than constraining only one behavior. The phenomenon and mechanism are both definite, and a component-wise negative result could rule out language-conditioned deception, monitor degradation, or causal mediation, although falsifying the conjunction alone would not justify the claim's stronger statement that "honesty is language-independent." In the topic-substitution check, replacing these specific coupled predictions with the generic language–AI relationship would not earn this score; the increment comes from the competence-controlled ordering and shared causal mediator.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: "language-conditioned honesty audits and CoT monitors" and an "honesty/self-monitoring direction" that can be steered to restore honesty, with the latter operating ex ante during generation rather than merely explaining deception afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction still travels as a relation—non-dominant-language reasoning should reduce signal engagement, increase deception, and reduce monitor recall—so it supplies more than a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction. Its asserted scope covers "several open-weight multilingual models," multiple lower-resource languages, and several deception settings, while downstream users include auditors and deployers deciding whether an English-only monitor can gate multilingual systems; nevertheless, transfer to closed frontier systems and natural deployments is not itself asserted. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic language–intelligence topic supplies neither the language-conditioned audit rule nor the inference-time steering handle.
